title: Quantized files: fp8, GGUF, and how loaders treat them

questions.q: Which file needs a pack to load in ComfyUI v0.43.0?
options: A safetensors file with comfy_quant entries
questions.why: Core's model folders do not list .gguf.

questions.q: You have an fp16 file and little VRAM. What is the first thing to try, with no new file?
questions.why: It sets the storage type at load from a file of any float type.

questions.q: Your card can't compute a format in a native quantized file. What happens?
options: Those layers keep small storage and dequantize for the multiply
questions.answer: Those layers keep small storage and dequantize for the multiply
questions.why: The console lists them as emulated ops.

questions.q: In the lab, why is the add-difference term so damaged by fp8 inputs?
options: Subtracting similar models leaves a small result, and the rounding errors stay their full size
The lab uses too few weights
questions.answer: Subtracting similar models leaves a small result, and the rounding errors stay their full size
questions.why: The error was 12% of the difference, against none from unquantized inputs.

questions.q: What is the order for merging and quantizing?
options: Merge unquantized files, then quantize the result once
Quantize each, merge, then quantize again
questions.answer: Merge unquantized files, then quantize the result once
questions.why: Rounding is permanent. Keep the arithmetic on the full numbers.

questions.q: When does a plain fp8 file stay fp8 in unet_dtype?
options: When the card computes fp8, or twice the parameters would not fit
questions.answer: When the card computes fp8, or twice the parameters would not fit
questions.why: Otherwise unet_dtype falls through to other types.
